notes: Abel's suggestion for Phase 3's missing real-jump test: rather than wait for a natural fast jump during play, step detector-passthrough's host-controlled overall gain sharply above unity to manufacture one. Two trials, both real growth confirmed on hardware, NEITHER armed the existing growth-rate detector. Trial 1 (gain 0.2->5.0): out_peak climbed -86dBFS->-13..-18dBFS within 3s -- fast and real, but analyse_take showed mean_partials=6.23, dominance=6.8dB: a broadband many-partials-at-once explosion, not a single partial jumping. The prominence-gated detector correctly does not fire on that -- it is not the scenario it is built for. Trial 2 (gain 0.2->1.3): out_peak climbed -84dBFS->~-34dBFS over 20s, plateauing -- analyse_take confirmed a genuinely clean single-partial event this time (dominance=103.8dB, stability=0.1 cents, mean_partials=1.17, 579.2Hz). This IS the target scenario and it still did not arm. Diagnosis: kArmGrowthDbPerFrame=0.8 (~138dB/s sustained 11.6ms, bela/detector-passthrough/render.cpp) was set from ground-rules-7's theoretical ~100-1000dB/s estimate for loop_gain~1.4; this rig's actual measured growth on a clean, unambiguous, real single-partial jump averaged only ~2.5dB/s. Per CLAUDE.md rule 16's spirit, the threshold is the more likely thing to revisit, not this test. Left open, not retuned here -- flagged for whenever Phase 3 detection work resumes; Phase 4 (the one-cell regulator) is next per Abel.
